why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief repeats the verifier's probe inputs and their expected outputs. In Step 1 it gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'", and Step 3 repeats "('42', 5 -> '00042')". Verifier Check 1 calls exactly padLeft('42',5,'0') and padLeft('ab',4) and needs "00042" and "  ab" to pass. Step 3 also lists the same cases as Check 2: s exactly width long and s longer than width, both unchanged. So the builder gets part of the checker's input/expected-output set, which the criterion forbids. Telling the builder to run npm test and to write tests is allowed. The overlapping concrete probes are not.
